views.title: Repository topology
views.purpose: Directory and file structure of the pinned repository, bounded to the dominant source areas.

views.title: Dependency surface
views.purpose: Observed import/dependency relationships, including external dependencies referenced by sampled source files.

views.title: Evidence map
views.purpose: The exact sampled source evidence used by the Atlas agents, anchored to the pinned source SHA.

views.title: Architecture clusters
views.purpose: Semantic component boundaries curated from the deterministic repository graph and source evidence.

views.title: Reading path
views.purpose: A curated order for understanding the repository without reading the codebase linearly.

views.title: Internal Module Dependency Graph
views.purpose: Show which source modules import which internal modules, revealing the hub-and-spoke architecture with server.py as the central orchestrator and service.py as the secondary business-logic hub. Answers: what is the internal code structure and which modules depend on which?

views.title: Think Tool Request Lifecycle
views.purpose: Trace a think_<mode> MCP tool call from server entry through guard check, template filling from modes data, JSONL store append with fsync, optional hook firing, and response return. Answers: what is the exact runtime path of a thinking tool call through the system?

views.title: Test-to-Source Coverage Map
views.purpose: Map each test module to the source module(s) it exercises, revealing the 1:1 coverage pattern and the two test files (test_server, test_service) that additionally cover secondary modules. Answers: what source modules are tested and by which test files?

views.title: Mode Data-to-Tool Registration Pipeline
views.purpose: Show how a mode entry in modes.json flows through modes.py (load, validate, register) to server.py (expose as think_<mode> MCP tool) and ultimately to service.py (template filling at call time). Answers: how does a JSON data entry become a callable MCP tool with no code change?

views.title: Data Persistence & Rotation Lifecycle
views.purpose: Focus on the store.py persistence hub and its interactions with service.py (write path), config.py (rotation threshold, state dir), hooks.py (post-store trigger), and modes.json (note attribution). Shows how notes are written with fsync, how rotation is triggered by file size, and how journal read-back works. Answers: how are thinking notes stored, rotated, and retrieved?
